features.summary: A plugin's declaration and the page's plugin: a JavaScript object the page's own code provides by name, with no element, for work the DSL does not express. Its declaration is a Plugin, named once with a vendor's characters and no dot, so the alis. names stay the framework's, and named with its listening, EventTarget unless an EventListening names a callback property, a method pair or a returned unsubscriber; its members are the whole declaration vocabulary, and CallItself calls a plugin that is a function. The page provides it by pushing a name and an instance onto window.__alisPlugins: boot reads the queue, and a later push registers at once. A name no script provides, or two provide, stops only the steps that reach it, and the page's other pipelines run. One plugin name is one object in a plan, with one listening (M13.D1). Main declares a plugin's members by strings, inline or on its Plugin, with argument shapes checked where the view renders, and registers it on the plan; the redesign declares it as a JsObject registered with RegisterPlugin<TPlugin>(), which raises no events; both stop the page's start for a name provided twice.

meanings.meaning: A plugin's name names one object in a plan, and the plan writes one locator for it, whatever reaches it: each declaration of that name, reached by a step or a handler, and a vendor's lookup by that name (N17.6). Two declarations of one name are two views of that object, each reaching the members it declares. Only a declaration that declares an event has its listening read (X17.45), so the locator carries the listening of the declarations of that name that declare one, and EventTarget when none does; a declaration that declares no event and a vendor's lookup add no listening. Two declarations of one name that each declare an event and whose listening differs are refused: at build by ALIS034 when both are constants of one compilation, and where the view renders when one plan reaches both, naming both declarations.

features.oracle: ECMAScript's typeof, property read and call, by which a provided instance is any value and a member a number lacks reads undefined; the DOM Standard's EventTarget; C#'s new() constraint and a protected base constructor, by which the core makes a declaration with new T() (D5.12); and the page's queue, an array the page's code pushes onto before boot and a push the runtime takes after it (D17.14).

defects.defect: Two declarations of one plugin name that each declare an event and whose listening differs both render, and the plan's one locator for the name carries the listening the last reach wrote, as the POC writes it (poc/Alis.Reactive.Poc/Writing/PlanBuild.cs:436-441), so the other declaration's handlers listen by a kind their object does not raise by and never run (M13.D1). ALIS034 (N18.12) reports two constant declarations of one name, each declaring an event, whose listening differs in one compilation; where the view renders, a plan that reaches both is refused, naming both declarations.

A declaration that declares no event, or a vendor's lookup, reached after a declaration of one name that declares one writes its EventTarget over that declaration's listening, so the event's handlers listen by a kind their object does not raise by (M13.D1).

promises.page: A visitor desk page whose VisitorBook : Plugin("visitorbook") declares Visits, a ReadOnly<int>, and Signed, an Event. The desk's script holds the book, an EventTarget whose visits is 3, and provides nothing at boot: its button Open the visitor book pushes {"name": "visitorbook", "instance": book} onto window.__alisPlugins and then writes book ready into book-state, and its button Sign the book dispatches signed on the book and writes signed into book-own. The view's buttons: Count the visits writes tried into count-tried, then the book's Visits into visits, then counted into count-done; Greet the visitor writes welcome into greeting. The book's Signed handler writes signed into book-signed.
promises.gesture: Click Count the visits and Greet the visitor; click Open the visitor book and wait until book-state reads book ready; click Count the visits; click Sign the book and wait until book-own reads signed.
promises.outcome: After the first Count the visits count-tried reads tried, and visits and count-done are empty; greeting reads welcome; after the second Count the visits visits reads 3 and count-done reads counted; after Sign the book book-own reads signed and book-signed is empty.
promises.opposite: The same desk whose script pushes the book as it loads, before the runtime boots: Count the visits writes 3 into visits and counted into count-done at the first click, and Sign the book writes signed into book-signed.
promises.defect: The redesign deletes the queue at boot (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/root.ts:44-45 at 65fdf118d), so the push of Open the visitor book is dropped with no word and the second Count the visits stops again: visits and count-done stay empty. A runtime that subscribes a plan's handlers when their plugin arrives writes signed into book-signed.

promises.page: A night ward page whose layout loads three scripts before the runtime: the ward's pushes {"name": "shiftlog"} with entries 2, the agency's pushes {"name": "shiftlog"} with entries 9, and the lantern's pushes {"name": "lantern", "instance": 42}. ShiftLog declares Entries, a ReadOnly<int>; Lantern : Plugin("lantern") declares Colour, a ReadOnly<string>. The page's load writes the page started into started. Read the log writes tried into log-tried, then the log's Entries into entries, then read into log-done; Read the lantern writes tried into lantern-tried, then the lantern's Colour into colour, then read into lantern-done; Start the round writes started into round.
promises.gesture: Click Read the log, Read the lantern and Start the round, then Read the log again.
promises.outcome: started reads the page started; after each Read the log log-tried reads tried, and entries and log-done are empty; lantern-tried reads tried, and colour and lantern-done are empty; round reads started.
promises.opposite: The same page with the agency's script left out and the lantern provided as {"colour": "amber"}: Read the log writes 2 into entries and read into log-done, and Read the lantern writes amber into colour and read into lantern-done.
promises.defect: The redesign stops the whole page for a name provided twice and for a value that is no object (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/objects/plugins.ts:24 and Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/objects/plugins.ts:35 at 65fdf118d), so started stays empty and no button runs, which its tests WhenThePageMeetsAPluginItCannotUse.a_plugin_name_a_second_bundle_registers_again_stops_the_page_from_starting and a_plugin_a_bundle_registers_as_something_that_holds_no_members_stops_the_page_from_starting assert and this promise flips. A registry that keeps the first provide writes 2 into entries, and one that keeps the last writes 9.

promises.page: A night desk page whose script provides nightclock before the runtime boots: a plain object with no addEventListener, holding hour "12", that calls its onStruck property when the clock's own button Strike midnight is clicked. NightClock : Plugin("nightclock", EventListening.CallbackProperties) declares Struck, an Event heard through onStruck, and its handler writes midnight into clock-struck; NightClockFace : Plugin("nightclock") declares Hour, a ReadOnly<string>, and no event. Rendered after the clock's handler, the button Read the hour writes the face's Hour into hour.
promises.gesture: Click Read the hour, then Strike midnight.
promises.outcome: hour reads 12 and clock-struck reads midnight.
promises.opposite: The same page with the button Read the hour rendered before the clock's handler: the same clicks write 12 into hour and midnight into clock-struck, so the order the view writes its reaches in does not decide the clock's listening.
promises.defect: The plan's one locator for nightclock carries the listening of the reach the view wrote last, as the POC writes it (poc/Alis.Reactive.Poc/Writing/PlanBuild.cs:439), so NightClockFace's EventTarget replaces NightClock's callback property; the handler looks for addEventListener on a clock that lacks it and does not start (D12.8), and clock-struck stays empty. A vendor's lookup by a plugin's name writes the same locator with EventTarget (poc/Alis.Reactive.Poc/Writing/PlanBuild.cs:419, poc/Alis.Reactive.Poc/Components/Component.cs:128), the same defect.

promises.page: A shift log page whose script provides four plugins on window.__alisPlugins before the runtime boots. shiftlog is an EventTarget holding entries, a number that starts at 0, add(note), which adds 1 to entries, and label(resident), which answers the resident followed by ": " and the entries; its declaration ShiftLog : Plugin("shiftlog") declares Entries, a Property<int>; Add(Arg<string> note), a Method; Label(Arg<string> resident), a Method<string>; and Signed, an Event. nightclock is declared Plugin("nightclock", EventListening.CallbackProperties) with Struck, an Event heard through its onStruck property. bedstore is declared Plugin("bedstore", EventListening.ReturnedUnsubscriber("subscribe")) with Freed, an Event<BedFreed> with a string Bed, its subscribe returning its unsubscribe. initials is a function that answers a name's initials, declared Plugin("initials") with Of(Arg<string> name) => CallItself<string>([name]). The script wires three buttons of its own: Sign the log dispatches signed on the shift log, Strike midnight calls the clock's onStruck, and Free bed 4 calls each freed subscriber with {"bed": "4"}. The view's buttons: Add a note calls Add("fed") and writes Entries into entries; Set the entries to 5 writes 5 into Entries and Entries into entries; Check the log, when Entries is greater than 5, calls Add("checked") and writes Entries into entries and busy into log-state, and otherwise writes quiet into log-state; Draw the dose chart draws a dose chart the app brings, with the ticks Ada and Bea, whose TickLabel, a Callback<TickArgs, string>, answers tick => shiftlog.Label(tick.Resident); Read the initials writes initials.Of("Ada Lovelace") into initials-read. The handlers: the shift log's Signed writes signed into log-signed, the clock's Struck writes midnight into clock-struck, and the bed store's Freed writes the payload's Bed into bed-freed.
promises.gesture: Click Add a note and Check the log; click Set the entries to 5, Add a note, Check the log and Draw the dose chart; click Read the initials; click Sign the log, Strike midnight and Free bed 4.
promises.outcome: After the first Check the log entries reads 1 and log-state reads quiet; after the second entries reads 7 and log-state reads busy; the dose chart's ticks read Ada: 7 and Bea: 7; initials-read reads AL; log-signed reads signed, clock-struck reads midnight and bed-freed reads 4.
promises.opposite: Reload the page and click Check the log first: log-state reads quiet and entries stays empty, since the term read 0 and no branch called Add.
promises.defect: A page's plugin is an object with no subscribe (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/objects/plugins.ts:36 at 65fdf118d) whose handler the redesign subscribes through that member (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/objects/plan-objects.ts:61 at 65fdf118d), so no handler of a plugin starts and log-signed, clock-struck and bed-freed stay empty. A runtime that listens to a plugin by EventTarget whatever its declaration names leaves clock-struck and bed-freed empty while log-signed reads signed.
